function: Transmit antenna selection: a DNN classifier predicts the active dual-polarized antenna combination from the channel matrix, replacing exhaustive search (pp. 1, 7-8).
system: Dual-polarized antennas, Nt = 4 or 8 at the transmitter; reflecting RIS with N = 32 elements (8 to 128 varied) split in B regions; frequency band not stated (pp. 3, 9).
method: Fully connected DNN classifier, three hidden layers (four neurons stated, G = 8 also given), ReLU, sigmoid output; supervised with cross-entropy loss and AdaGrad (pp. 8-9).
data_channel: Own simulator: Rayleigh and Rician (K = 1) fading with cross-polar discrimination, perfect CSI at the receiver; 25600 generated channel samples for training, validation and test (pp. 4, 8, 9).
test_conditions: Trained and tested on the same channel type, with or without RIS; test set is 0.1 of the same generated samples; Nt = 4 and 8 are separate setups (p. 9).
baselines: Only exhaustive full-traversal conventional TAS for the DNN; polarization modulation and ML detection for the non-learned scheme I; no learned baseline (pp. 6, 9, 10).
metrics: BER, spectral efficiency (bits/s/Hz), and complexity of antenna selection and of detection (pp. 6, 9, 10).
complexity: DNN prediction cost Nt^2 G + (L-1) G^2 Nt^2 + (G+1) T versus Nt^3 Nr^2 M^2 for conventional TAS; Fig. 8 plots both; detection flops in Table III (pp. 6, 8, 10).
q1_support: p. 4: "the entire channel environment is characterized by Rayleigh fading". Custom simulator with Rayleigh and Rician fading (p. 8); no 3GPP, COST 2100, DeepMIMO or measured data, so not met.
q2_support: p. 9: "even if the number of DP-AEs changes" only says each antenna count has enough training samples; the test split is held out from the same data ("of which 0.2 are designated as the validation set"). No train-test mismatch is reported.
q3_support: p. 10: "BER of TAS between the conventional schemes and the proposed" DNN-based schemes (Figs. 6 and 7): only exhaustive TAS, which is non-learned. No earlier learned antenna selector (SVM, KNN, naive Bayes cited on p. 2) or standard network is compared.
q4_support: p. 8: "the complexity for prediction of the DNN schemes is given by" Nt^2 G + (L-1) G^2 Nt^2 + (G+1) T, against Nt^3 Nr^2 M^2 for the conventional scheme; compared in Fig. 8 (p. 10).
q5_support: p. 9: "The training set comprises a total of 25600 training samples," generated by the authors' own channel simulator; no code or data link, DOI or public dataset appears anywhere in the paper.
notes: Title on p. 1 matches the DOI. Two schemes: scheme I (polarization index modulation with RIS region index, ML or stepwise detection) is not learned; only scheme II, the DNN antenna selection, is learned. RIS phase shifts are set analytically (p. 5), not learned. Area 3 is borderline: transmit antenna selection is taken as a discrete transmit precoder (selection matrix, p. 3), so the reviewer should confirm it is not excluded as link adaptation. q4 counts the DNN prediction cost of Eq. (50).
